actions.create_bill.description: Creates a vendor bill (accounts payable) in QuickBooks Desktop, expensed against one or more accounts.
actions.create_bill.props.dueDate.descri: When left blank, QuickBooks Desktop derives it from the vendor's default payment terms.
actions.create_bill.props.expenseLines.d: At least one expense line is required. Each line expenses this bill against one Chart of Accounts entry (e.g. fuel, maintenance, insurance) — not a product/service item.
actions.create_bill.props.memo.descripti: Internal note. Appears in the A/P register and reports, not sent to the vendor.
actions.create_bill.props.refNumber.desc: Optional reference number (max 20 characters). QuickBooks Desktop does not auto-generate one if left blank.
actions.create_bill.props.vendorId.descr: The vendor this bill is from. Only vendors that already exist in QuickBooks Desktop appear here — use Upsert Vendor first if the vendor might not exist yet.
actions.create_invoice.description: Creates an invoice for a customer in QuickBooks Desktop.
The customer this invoice is for. Only customers that already exist in QuickBooks Desktop appear here — use Upsert Customer first if the customer might not exist yet.
actions.create_invoice.props.dueDate.des: When left blank, QuickBooks Desktop derives it from the customer's default payment terms.
actions.create_invoice.props.lineItems.d: At least one line item is required.
actions.create_invoice.props.memo.descri: Internal note. Appears in reports, not on the invoice sent to the customer.
actions.create_invoice.props.refNumber.d: Optional reference number (max 11 characters). QuickBooks Desktop does not auto-generate one if left blank.
actions.custom_api_call.description: Make a custom API call to a specific endpoint
actions.custom_api_call.props.failsafe.d: On a failed request, output the error instead of failing the step.
actions.custom_api_call.props.followRedi: Follow 3xx redirects instead of returning them as the response.
actions.custom_api_call.props.headers.de: Authorization headers are injected automatically from your connection.
actions.custom_api_call.props.response_i: Enable for files like PDFs, images, etc.
actions.custom_api_call.props.timeout.de: Seconds to wait for a response. Empty: up to the flow limit (10 min).
actions.list_items.description: Lists Service and Non-Inventory items from QuickBooks Desktop, for finding the exact item name to use in Create Invoice's line items.
actions.list_items.props.limit.descripti: Results per item type — up to twice this many total, since Service and Non-Inventory items are searched together (1–150).
actions.list_items.props.nameContains.de: Search by a substring of the item name. Leave empty to list all items.
actions.query_transactions.description: Searches across all transaction types in QuickBooks Desktop (invoices, bills, payments, and more) with date and type filters.
Optional. Pass the Next Cursor from a previous call's output to fetch the next page.
actions.query_transactions.props.entityI: Optional. A customer, vendor, or employee id to filter by — typically chained from another step's output (e.g. Upsert Customer's Customer ID), not typed by hand.
actions.query_transactions.props.payment: Leave empty to search regardless of payment status.
actions.query_transactions.props.transac: Leave empty to search all types.
actions.record_payment.description: Records a customer payment against open invoices, or a vendor bill payment by check or credit card, in QuickBooks Desktop.
actions.record_payment.props.applyToSpec: Customer Payment only. When off, QuickBooks Desktop automatically applies the payment to an exact-amount match or the oldest open invoice.
actions.record_payment.props.bankAccount: Required for Bill Payment — Check only. The account funds are drawn from.
actions.record_payment.props.billId.desc: Required for both Bill Payment types. QuickBooks Desktop has no auto-apply for bill payments, so the specific open bill must be picked.
actions.record_payment.props.creditCardA: Required for Bill Payment — Credit Card only. The account charged.
Required for Customer Payment only. The customer who made this payment.
actions.record_payment.props.invoiceId.d: The specific open invoice this payment applies to.
actions.record_payment.props.paymentType: Vendor Bill Payment — Credit Card (Accounts Payable)
actions.record_payment.props.refNumber.d: Optional. Max 20 characters for a customer payment, max 11 for a bill payment (it's the check number for a check payment).
actions.record_payment.props.vendorId.de: Required for both Bill Payment types. The vendor being paid.
actions.upsert_customer.description: Creates a customer in QuickBooks Desktop, or updates it if one with the same name already exists.
actions.upsert_customer.props.name.descr: The exact name of the customer as it should appear in QuickBooks Desktop (max 41 characters). Used to find an existing customer — if one already exists with this exact name, it is updated instead of duplicated.
actions.upsert_vendor.description: Creates a vendor in QuickBooks Desktop, or updates it if one with the same name already exists.
actions.upsert_vendor.props.name.descrip: The exact name of the vendor as it should appear in QuickBooks Desktop (max 41 characters, unique across all vendors). Used to find an existing vendor — if one already exists with this exact name, it is updated instead of duplicated.
auth.description:
This piece connects to QuickBooks Desktop through [Conductor](https://conductor.is) — Activepieces
cannot talk to QuickBooks Desktop directly, since it has no cloud API of its own.

1. In your Conductor dashboard, go to **Settings → API Keys** and copy your **Secret Key**.
2. Under **End-Users**, select (or create) the end-user connected to this QuickBooks Desktop
   company file and copy their **End-User ID** (starts with `end_usr_`).
3. The end-user must have already completed Conductor's auth flow and installed the QuickBooks
   Web Connector — Conductor's dashboard shows the connection as "Connected" once QuickBooks
   Desktop is reachable. If it shows "Not connected," fix that in Conductor before connecting here.
4. **Top setup mistake — read before finishing step 3:** when QuickBooks Desktop first asks to
   authorize the Web Connector, **choose the option that keeps access even when QuickBooks Desktop
   isn't running** (not "ask every time"). Picking the wrong option doesn't error — it just makes
   every sync silently do nothing until someone is sitting at the QuickBooks Desktop machine to
   approve it, which usually isn't noticed until a customer asks why nothing has synced in days.
   See this piece's README for the full walkthrough.
auth.props.endUserId.description: The end-user ID for this QuickBooks Desktop company file (starts with end_usr_).
auth.props.secretKey.description: From your Conductor dashboard, Settings → API Keys.
description: Sync invoices, bills, customers, vendors and payments with QuickBooks Desktop through the Conductor API bridge.
triggers.new_or_updated_invoice.descript: Fires when an invoice is created or updated (e.g. line items, balance, or payment status changed) in QuickBooks Desktop. One event per invoice change, not create-only.
triggers.new_payment.description: Fires once when a new customer payment is recorded (Accounts Receivable) in QuickBooks Desktop — a "Receive Payment" transaction, e.g. from the Record Payment action's Customer Payment mode. Create-only: editing an existing payment does not re-fire it. Vendor bill payments (Accounts Payable) do not fire this trigger.
